title: 1.1 Definition of Common Terms
description: Key terms in crop production and the hunter-gatherer history

questions.question: How is agriculture defined in the handout?
options: The accidental collection of wild plants and occasional hunting of animals
The gathering of plant products from the wild for immediate use
The process of clearing forests for natural regeneration of plants
The deliberate cultivation of crops and rearing of animals
questions.correctAnswer: The deliberate cultivation of crops and rearing of animals

questions.question: Before the introduction of agriculture, how did societies survive?
options: By cultivating large areas of cereals every year
By trading manufactured goods with neighbouring groups
By hunting animals and gathering plants for food
By practising settled irrigation farming
questions.correctAnswer: By hunting animals and gathering plants for food

questions.question: According to studies, what was required for hunter-gatherers to survive?
options: They had to rely only on luck
They had to use advanced machinery
They had to form large empires
They had to be insightful
questions.correctAnswer: They had to be insightful

questions.question: What happened to the hunter-gatherer lifestyle with the expansion of agriculture?
options: It completely disappeared within a few decades
It was immediately replaced in all parts of the world
It ended completely before the start of settled agriculture
It has not completely disappeared with the expansion of agriculture
questions.correctAnswer: It has not completely disappeared with the expansion of agriculture

questions.question: Where can hunter-gatherers still be found today according to the handout?
options: In the most fertile river valleys where crop production is very high
In areas where the land and climate conditions do not favor deliberate crop culture
In regions with well-developed irrigation systems
In all highland areas with sufficient rainfall
questions.correctAnswer: In areas where the land and climate conditions do not favor deliberate crop culture

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of places where hunter-gatherers still exist?
options: Well-drained volcanic highlands with high yields
Major river deltas used for intensive rice production
Desert areas, Arctic region and pockets of tropical rain forest
Temperate grasslands with heavy annual rainfall
questions.correctAnswer: Desert areas, Arctic region and pockets of tropical rain forest

questions.question: Why did people first start to domesticate animals before agriculture became widespread?
options: Mainly for producing electricity
Mainly for constructing modern buildings
Mainly for food production
Mainly for exporting to other regions
questions.correctAnswer: Mainly for food production

questions.question: For what purpose did people later breed animals, in addition to food production?
options: To produce non-food materials
To develop chemical fertilizers
To increase internet connectivity
To create digital records
questions.correctAnswer: To produce non-food materials

questions.question: What has gradually become the major means of survival for societies?
options: Trading rare stones only
Hunting and gathering alone
Crop and livestock production
Raiding neighbouring communities
questions.correctAnswer: Crop and livestock production

questions.question: What is shifting cultivation?
options: A system of growing different crops at the same time in permanent irrigation fields
A form of agriculture in which an area of ground is cleared of vegetation and cultivated for a few years and then abandoned for a new area
A form of settled farming where the same plot is cultivated continuously for decades without rest
A method where crops are planted only in greenhouses with artificial soil
questions.correctAnswer: A form of agriculture in which an area of ground is cleared of vegetation and cultivated for a few years and then abandoned for a new area

questions.question: How long was land cultivated under early shifting cultivation?
options: For at least five full decades
For fifty years continuously
For ten to fifteen consecutive years
Just one or two seasons
questions.correctAnswer: Just one or two seasons

questions.question: What common practice was associated with shifting cultivation?
options: Building permanent terraces and never moving to new land
Abandoning the land cultivated after it had been cultivated once and shifting to a new location
Keeping all plots under continuous irrigation every year
Maintaining the same field permanently with no change of location
questions.correctAnswer: Abandoning the land cultivated after it had been cultivated once and shifting to a new location

questions.question: What is settled agriculture?
options: The practice of depending entirely on wild plant collection year after year
The practice of using the same plot of land continuously over a long period to grow crops or rear livestock
The practice of clearing new land every season and never returning
The practice of growing crops only in natural forests without clearing
questions.correctAnswer: The practice of using the same plot of land continuously over a long period to grow crops or rear livestock

questions.question: How is land cultivated in settled agriculture?
options: The land is left untouched for most years and cultivated randomly
The land is cultivated continuously
The land is cultivated only once in twenty years
The land is cultivated for one season and never used again
questions.correctAnswer: The land is cultivated continuously

questions.question: What type of practices are associated with settled agriculture?
options: Only harvesting without any land management
Yield enhancing practices
Practices that deliberately lower crop yields
Practices that avoid adding any organic matter to soil
questions.correctAnswer: Yield enhancing practices

questions.question: Which of the following is a yield enhancing practice mentioned for settled agriculture?
options: Leaving the land bare with no inputs
Burning all crop residues without return
Using manure
Removing all topsoil every year
questions.correctAnswer: Using manure

questions.question: Which yield enhancing practice is mentioned for settled agriculture?
options: Using fertilizer
Deliberately overgrazing all fields
Cutting down all vegetation and leaving soil exposed permanently
Avoiding any form of soil protection
questions.correctAnswer: Using fertilizer

questions.question: Which soil protection practice is associated with settled agriculture?
options: Removing all soil cover every season
Allowing uncontrolled water flow across fields
Ploughing straight down steep slopes with no barriers
The construction of soil bunds for erosion control
questions.correctAnswer: The construction of soil bunds for erosion control

questions.question: What aspect of water use is associated with settled agriculture?
options: The optimized use of water
Wasting water by uncontrolled flooding with no control
Never considering water availability for crops
Complete abandonment of water management
questions.correctAnswer: The optimized use of water

questions.question: How does settled agriculture compare to traditional shifting cultivation?
options: They are exactly the same in all respects
Settled agriculture is only used where shifting cultivation cannot be practised
Settled agriculture is a more advanced activity than traditional shifting cultivation
Settled agriculture is less advanced than traditional shifting cultivation
questions.correctAnswer: Settled agriculture is a more advanced activity than traditional shifting cultivation

questions.question: What is subsistence farming?
options: A situation in which a farmer produces crops and livestock sufficient only for household use without any surplus for trade
A type of farming where all produce is sold for profit in large markets
A system focused entirely on producing crops for industrial processing only
A large-scale commercial farming system using heavy machinery for export
questions.correctAnswer: A situation in which a farmer produces crops and livestock sufficient only for household use without any surplus for trade

questions.question: What is the major aim of subsistence farming?
options: To maximize export earnings for the national economy
To produce crops and animals for the farmer’s own consumption
To produce only non-food cash crops for international markets
To supply large agro-industries with raw materials for profit
questions.correctAnswer: To produce crops and animals for the farmer’s own consumption

questions.question: What kind of techniques does subsistence farming often require?
options: Sophisticated laboratory-based techniques for every operation
Very advanced industrial techniques requiring large capital
Simple techniques that often do not go beyond a household capacity
Highly automated techniques using satellite-guided machinery
questions.correctAnswer: Simple techniques that often do not go beyond a household capacity

questions.question: If there is any excess production in subsistence farming, what might happen to it?
options: It might be stored for times of poor harvest or sold to generate income for the household
It is exported directly by the government without household benefit
It is discarded as waste without any use
It is always destroyed to keep market prices high
questions.correctAnswer: It might be stored for times of poor harvest or sold to generate income for the household

questions.question: Which statement best describes shifting cultivation in terms of duration of use?
options: Land is cultivated every year for over twenty years in the same place
Land is used continuously for many decades without shifting
Land is cultivated for just one or two seasons before shifting
Land is used for three to five years and then kept permanently
questions.correctAnswer: Land is cultivated for just one or two seasons before shifting

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a yield enhancing practice in settled agriculture?
options: Building dams for hydroelectric power
Leaving the land to the wild for many years
Using manure and fertilizer
Clearing new land every season
questions.correctAnswer: Using manure and fertilizer

questions.question: What is the main distinction between shifting cultivation and settled agriculture regarding land use?
options: Both use the same plot continuously with identical practices
Shifting cultivation uses the same plot continuously, settled agriculture moves every season
Both abandon land permanently after first cultivation
Shifting cultivation moves to new land after a few years, settled agriculture uses the same plot continuously
questions.correctAnswer: Shifting cultivation moves to new land after a few years, settled agriculture uses the same plot continuously

questions.question: Which activity is described as a more advanced activity than traditional shifting cultivation?
options: Settled agriculture
Unplanned clearing of land every season
Random gathering of wild plants
Primitive hunting without tools
questions.correctAnswer: Settled agriculture

questions.question: In subsistence farming, the produce is primarily intended for whom?
options: Government stockpiles for international trade
Large export companies
Industrial food processors for mass markets
The farmer’s own household consumption
questions.correctAnswer: The farmer’s own household consumption

questions.question: According to the handout, when might subsistence farmers sell excess production?
options: To control global food prices
To generate income for the household
To supply all regional supermarkets
To meet national export quotas only
questions.correctAnswer: To generate income for the household
